comment: Common (cross-version) manual corrections for known perl C-source bugs that cause incorrect Rust binding generation. Loaded for every perl version; per-version overrides go in v$X.$Y.patches.json (kind: "remove" cancels a common entry for that version). See src/apidoc_patches.rs for the schema and doc/architecture-apidoc-patches.md for the merge model.

patches.name: RCPV_LEN
patches.reason: perl cop.h apidoc declares `RCPV *` but the macro body `(RCPVx(pv)->len-1)` returns STRLEN (a usize), not a pointer. The apidoc return type is wrong.

patches.name: RCPV_REFCOUNT
patches.reason: perl cop.h apidoc declares `RCPV *` but the macro body `(RCPVx(pv)->refcount)` returns STRLEN (the refcount field), not a pointer.

patches.name: RCPV_REFCNT_inc
patches.reason: perl cop.h apidoc declares `RCPV *` but the macro body calls rcpv_copy(pv) which returns `char *` per proto.h.

patches.name: RCPV_REFCNT_dec
patches.reason: perl cop.h apidoc declares `RCPV *` but the macro body calls rcpv_free(pv) which returns `char *` per proto.h.

patches.name: Perl_custom_op_xop
patches.reason: perl op.h macro definition `(Perl_custom_op_get_field(x, XOPe_xop_ptr).xop_ptr)` lacks `aTHX_`. The function expects 3 args (pTHX_ const OP *o, const xop_flags_enum field) but the macro only passes 2, causing Rust E0061 (function takes 3 arguments but 2 arguments were supplied). XopENTRYCUSTOM(o, xop_ptr) on line 967 is the correct alternative — it passes aTHX_ properly.

patches.reason: pad.h apidoc declares `PADLIST padlist` (missing `*`); the macro body passes it to PadlistARRAY() which takes `PADLIST *`.

patches.name: PadARRAY
patches.reason: pad.h apidoc in <=5.30 declares `PAD pad` (missing `*`); the macro body passes it to AvARRAY() which takes `AV *` (PAD = AV). Fixed upstream in 5.32 (`PAD * pad`) -- this override is identity there. Without it PadARRAY on <=5.30 is generated with a by-value `PAD` param (downstream E0308).

patches.name: MUTABLE_AV
patches.reason: handy.h apidoc declares the param with the target type, but the macro's real contract is `void *` -> cast: the body is `((T*)MUTABLE_PTR(p))` and callers pass unrelated pointer types (e.g. SAVECOMPPAD passes PAD* to MUTABLE_SV).

patches.name: AvFILL
patches.reason: av.h apidoc_defn declares SSize_t but the bundled apidoc data carries I32 (stale); the macro body branches yield SSize_t (AvFILLp / mg_size).

patches.name: MUTABLE_AV
patches.reason: =for apidoc declaration absent from headers before 5.34 (verified v5.32.0 handy.h has none); the macro itself and its contract are identical in older perls. Without the declaration, dependent macros (Cv/Hv family) cascade away on <=5.32. No-op on 5.34+. The companion arg_type_override (void *) still applies on top.

patches.name: MUTABLE_CV
patches.reason: =for apidoc declaration absent from headers before 5.34; contract identical in older perls. See MUTABLE_AV.

patches.name: MUTABLE_PTR
patches.reason: =for apidoc declaration absent from headers before 5.34; contract identical in older perls. Base macro of the MUTABLE_* family; its absence is the root of the Cv/Hv-family cascade on <=5.32. No arg override needed (header arg is already void *).

patches.name: MUTABLE_SV
patches.reason: =for apidoc declaration absent from headers before 5.34; contract identical in older perls. See MUTABLE_AV.

patches.name: AvARRAY
patches.reason: =for apidoc declaration absent from headers before 5.34 (verified v5.32.0 av.h); the macro and the xpvav layout are identical in older perls (xav_alloc/sv_u). Without it AvARRAY is mistyped downstream (E0308 on 5.30 libperl-sys).

patches.name: AvFILLp
patches.reason: =for apidoc declaration absent from headers <=5.30; 5.32 declares it as `int` (add_decl is a no-op there -- corrected by the companion return_type_override below). struct xpvav.xav_fill is SSize_t in all supported versions (verified v5.20.0/v5.32.0 av.h).

patches.name: AvFILLp
patches.reason: 5.32's av.h apidoc declares `int` but struct xpvav.xav_fill is SSize_t in all supported versions (verified v5.20.0/v5.32.0 sources); 5.34+ headers declare SSize_t. Identity for 5.34+ and for the injected add_decl.

patches.name: XopENTRY
patches.reason: op.h apidoc in <=5.36 declares the `which` param without the `token` type. The macro pastes it (`xop->xop_##which` style), so macrogen must inline-expand call sites instead of generating a callable fn; the `token` annotation (added upstream in 5.38: `Amu|...|token which`) is that signal. Identity on 5.38+.

patches.name: XopENTRYCUSTOM
patches.reason: op.h apidoc in <=5.36 lacks the `token` type on `which`; the macro pastes it (`XOPe_##which`), leaving XOPe_which unresolved when treated as a callable fn and cascading OP_CLASS/OP_DESC/OP_NAME away. See XopENTRY. Identity on 5.38+.

Note: CAT2/STRINGIFY were reviewed for the same class -- <=5.30 has no apidoc declaration at all (nothing to override) and 5.34+ already carries `token`, so no patch is needed for them.
